title: Executor
one_liner: The executor runs the planner's plan tree by pulling one row at a time from the top node down to the table scans.
analogy: A kitchen line: the head chef asks for one dish, each cook asks the cook before them, and the pantry hands over one item at a time.
big_picture: The planner makes a read-only Plan tree. The executor builds a matching PlanState tree for all changing data.
Execution is pull-based: the top node asks its children for one row, they ask theirs, down to the scans.
Every node has the same call shape: ExecProcNode(node) returns one TupleTableSlot, or an empty slot when done.
Rows travel in TupleTableSlots, a wrapper over a buffer tuple, heap tuple, minimal tuple or plain values.
WHERE clauses and target lists become flat ExprState step arrays. JIT can compile them to machine code for costly queries.
A Portal is the cursor-like object that drives the executor, so clients can fetch rows in batches.

flow.detail: PortalStart picks a strategy such as PORTAL_ONE_SELECT and calls executor startup.
Creates the EState (snapshot, memory context) and calls InitPlan.
ExecInitNode makes one PlanState per Plan node and sets its ExecProcNode function pointer.
Quals go through ExecInitQual and target lists through ExecBuildProjectionInfo. ExecReadyExpr picks the interpreter or a JIT function.
PortalRun calls ExecutorRun, which calls ExecutePlan to pull slots from the top node in a loop.
Each node calls ExecProcNode on its child, e.g. ExecHashJoin pulls from outer and hashed inner plans.
ExecutePlan hands each slot to the DestReceiver, which sends it to the client.
ExecutorFinish runs after-triggers. ExecutorEnd calls ExecEndPlan, which calls ExecEndNode to free everything.

diagram.claim: A Portal drives ExecutorRun, which pulls slots up through the PlanState tree from scans to the client.

interview.q: What does the executor do, and what does it get as input?
answer: It runs the plan the planner made and produces result rows.
Input is a PlannedStmt holding a Plan tree.
It also handles INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE via a ModifyTable node.
interview.trap: The executor does not choose the plan. That is the planner's job.

interview.q: What is the difference between a Plan node and a PlanState node?
answer: Plan nodes are read-only and made by the planner.
PlanState nodes mirror them and hold all runtime data.
Read-only plans can be cached and reused safely.
interview.trap: Plan and PlanState are not the same tree. They are parallel trees of equal shape.

answer: The top node asks for one row. It calls ExecProcNode on its child.
Each child does the same, down to a scan node.
A node returns one slot, or NULL or an empty slot at the end.
interview.trap: Rows are not pushed up in bulk. Each call yields a single row.

interview.q: How does ExecProcNode know which function to call?
answer: Each PlanState has an ExecProcNode function pointer set by ExecInitNode.
ExecSetExecProcNode first points it at ExecProcNodeFirst.
The first call checks stack depth, then swaps in the real function or ExecProcNodeInstr for EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
interview.trap: It is not a big switch on every call. It is a pointer set once.

interview.q: What is a TupleTableSlot and why does it exist?
answer: A slot is a container that passes one row between nodes.
It has types: TTSOpsBufferHeapTuple, TTSOpsHeapTuple, TTSOpsMinimalTuple, TTSOpsVirtual.
It lets nodes read columns without copying until needed.
interview.trap: A slot is not a tuple copy. It may just point into a buffer page.

interview.q: How do SeqScan and IndexScan share code?
answer: Both use ExecScan with an access method callback: SeqNext or IndexNext.
ExecScan applies the qual (WHERE) and the projection.
Only the way of fetching the next raw row differs.

interview.q: How does Hash Join work, and why is it a state machine?
answer: It first builds a hash table from the inner side (HJ_BUILD_HASHTABLE).
Then it reads outer rows and probes the table for matches.
It must remember where it was between calls, since it returns one row per call.
interview.trap: It is not a nested loop. Rows are matched by hash bucket, not by scanning all pairs.

interview.q: How are Sort and Agg different from scans?
answer: Sort is blocking: ExecSort reads all input into tuplesort, then returns rows in order.
Agg has strategies AGG_PLAIN, AGG_SORTED and AGG_HASHED.
These nodes may spill to disk when memory runs out.
interview.trap: Sort cannot return the first row before it reads all input.

interview.q: How are expressions evaluated and when does JIT kick in?
answer: ExecInitExpr, ExecInitQual and friends turn the tree into a flat steps array.
ExecInterpExpr runs the steps in one loop, no recursion.
The planner decides on JIT: standard_planner sets jitFlags when cost is above jit_above_cost (default 100000).
Then ExecReadyExpr may call llvm_compile_expr. This needs a build with LLVM.
interview.trap: JIT is not always faster. Compile time can cost more than it saves on cheap queries.

interview.q: What is a Portal and how does it relate to the executor?
answer: A Portal holds a query plus its execution state, like a cursor.
PortalRun calls ExecutorRun, optionally with a row count limit.
Strategies like PORTAL_ONE_SELECT allow fetching in batches; PORTAL_MULTI_QUERY runs everything at once.
interview.trap: Portals are not only for DECLARE CURSOR. Every query goes through one.

contributor_tips: Read src/backend/executor/README first, then nodeSeqscan.c. It is the smallest complete node.
Trace one SELECT in gdb from PortalRun down to SeqNext to see the pull model live.
Adding a node touches many places: Plan, PlanState, ExecInitNode, ExecProcNode, EXPLAIN. Mirror an existing small node.
Be careful with memory contexts and slot ownership. Many bugs are a slot pointing to freed data.

glossary.meaning: Runtime state for one plan node, with an ExecProcNode pointer.
Per-query executor state: snapshot, memory context, range table.
Container that carries one row between nodes.
Flat compiled form of one expression, stored in steps[].
Cursor-like object that holds a query and drives execution.
Compiles expressions to native code at run time using LLVM.

more: This is the Volcano or iterator model: one tuple per call.
ExprContext is reset after every tuple so per-row memory does not leak.
ModifyTable runs INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE, with RETURNING.
Gather and parallel workers; Hash batches and Sort spill to disk past work_mem.
Extensions hook in with ExecutorStart_hook and friends.
